## Redaction CPU bounds (R-4, `log-redactor.ts`, `error-sanitizer.ts`, `attributes.ts`)

- URI-userinfo rule: leading `` replaced by `(?<![A-Za-z0-9+.-])`; e-mail rule gets `(?<![A-Za-z0-9._%+-])`. Only the start of a run scans forward, so both are linear (the old forms took seconds on 64 KB of `a.`).
- Inputs are cut BEFORE redaction: error message 2048 chars (`MAX_MESSAGE_INPUT`; stored <= 1024), stack frame line 512 chars (`MAX_FRAME_INPUT`; stored <= 256), attribute string 1024 chars (`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_INPUT`; stored <= 256).
- A root-origin error is sanitized once (the root span and the trace share one payload object; `record-mapper.ts` caches by payload).
- `error-sanitizer.ts` cuts the stack header (name + message, possibly multi-line) before looking for `at ` frame lines, so a message line starting with `at ` is never stored as a frame.

## Notes for the README (O-5, inherited from upstream)

- Wrapping a `Promise` subclass or a promise with own properties (as `trace()` roots, joined spans and instrumented provider methods do) watches it on a side branch, which marks it handled: a rejection the caller drops no longer raises `unhandledRejection`. A bare native promise is replaced by a chained one and keeps the normal `unhandledRejection` behaviour.
- Error origin tracking compares thrown objects by reference and thrown primitives by value: two unrelated `throw 'x'` in one trace count as one error origin.
- Admission refusal by the global `maxOpenSpans` budget is treated like any other admission refusal: the root runs unsampled in a fresh store and `tracesDroppedAdmission` is counted (R-5).

- PEM private-key rule: the lazy regex `[sS]*?` was quadratic on repeated `-----BEGIN` markers without END (59-65 ms for 64 KB, flaky against a 50 ms budget). It is replaced by a linear scan (`redactPem`, indexOf + sticky regexes) that stops as soon as no END exists after a BEGIN. No body-length limit, so long keys are still redacted whole.

## Review round 2 (N-1, O-a, O-b)

- N-1: `redactPem` redacts an unterminated BEGIN (typically a key cut off by an input cap) from the BEGIN to the end of the text, instead of leaving it. Still linear.
- O-a: `capInput(text, max)` (error-sanitizer.ts, also used by attributes.ts) cuts to the cap and, when something was cut, drops the trailing partial token back to the last whitespace or delimiter, so a secret split at the cap (for example `mongodb://admin:hunter2@...` cut after `admin`) is never stored half-redacted. A cut text without any delimiter is kept as cut.
- O-b: the registry records `headerLines` (lines of the V8 stack header = lines of the uncapped message) in the error payload; the sanitizer skips exactly that many lines before taking `at ` frames, so a long message (over the 8192 raw cap) or a long class name can no longer put a message line into the stored stack. Hand-built payloads without `headerLines` fall back to locating the message at the top of the stack.

## Mission 03 (instrumentation hardening)

### Source changes to vendored or derived files

- `src/context/vendor/trace-registry.ts`, `pluckSnapshot` (O-2): the unconditional `setTimeout(completionTimeout)` wait is replaced by a waiter stored on the snapshot (`completionWaiter`). `completeNode` calls it when `refsCounter === refsMarkedAsComplete`, i.e. when the LAST open span ends, so the pluck resolves immediately; the 1000 ms timeout stays as the ceiling. The timer is `unref()`'d (a waiting pluck never keeps the process alive; `whenCompletionsIdle` owns the shutdown wait with a ref'd, bounded timer). Upstream waited the full timeout whenever any span was open.
- `src/context/root-runner.ts`: the raw `TraceOptions.attributes` copy at root start is replaced by `capRawAttributes` (`src/context/raw-attributes.ts`, new): at most 16 accepted keys, key pattern, strings cut to 1024 chars, finite numbers and booleans only, hostile objects (throwing getter or proxy trap) give `undefined`. Redaction still happens in the buffer.
- `src/context/completion.ts`: every completion start and finish goes through `completionStarted`/`completionFinished`; `whenCompletionsIdle(timeoutMs)` (new) resolves `true` when `pendingCompletions` reaches 0 and `false` on timeout, never rejects.

### New files (original Tracelet code, no upstream counterpart)

`src/buffer/histogram.ts`, `src/buffer/rollups.ts` (`RollupAccumulator`), `src/buffer/hooks.ts` (`createBufferHooks`), `src/context/raw-attributes.ts`.

### Mission 03 review follow-ups

- `src/context/raw-attributes.ts` slices strings to 1025 chars (ONE over the buffer's 1024 `capInput` cap) on purpose, so `capInput` still drops the trailing partial token and a secret split at the cut is never stored half-redacted (M-1). It scans at most 64 keys.
- `src/buffer/rollups.ts` keys operations by `kind NUL name.slice(0,256)` and methods by `operation` only, matching the storage `_id` formulas of the freeze doc (section 4); an auto span and a manual trace with the same name merge into one method row (M-2).
- `configureTracing`: the first call enables (default true), later calls without `enabled` keep the current value (a hooks-only call cannot undo a shutdown disable).
- `whenCompletionsIdle` clamps `Infinity` and anything above 2^31-1 ms to `MAX_IDLE_WAIT_MS`.
- **Runtime ABI policy:** `TRACELET_RUNTIME_ABI` (`src/shared/als.ts`) MUST be bumped on ANY change to the shape or behaviour of what is stored in the global slot (runtime fields, registry, token, store keys). It is now 2 (the runtime gained `idleWaiters` and `configured`).
